chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who appointed another as an agent in one of his affairs and had two witnesses testify to that, then the agent arose and went out to carry out the matter, and he said: Bear witness that I have dismissed so-and-so from the agency.

So he said: If the agent executed the matter for which he had been appointed before he was dismissed from the agency, then the matter is established and effective according to what the agent executed, whether the principal disliked it or was pleased.

I said: If the agent carried out the matter before he came to know of the dismissal, or before word reached him that he had been dismissed from the agency, then is the matter according to what he carried out? He said: Yes.

I said: Then if notice of dismissal reached him before he executed the matter, and he then went and carried it out, would that be of no effect? He said: Yes. Indeed, when an agent is appointed and then rises from the session, his authority remains effective forever, and the agency remains established until notice of dismissal from the agency reaches him through a trustworthy person who informs him, or he is directly addressed with the dismissal from the agency.

key_terms.أَمْضَى: he executed, carried out, or finalized the matter
key_terms.الْمُوَكِّلُ: the principal who appoints the agent
key_terms.الْوَكَالَةِ: agency or authorized representation in a legal matter
key_terms.الْوَكِيلُ: the appointed agent acting on behalf of another
key_terms.بِثِقَةٍ: through a trustworthy person whose report is relied upon
key_terms.ثَابِتَةٌ: legally established and remaining in force
key_terms.عَزَلْتُ: I dismissed or removed from office/agency

ai.seo_question: Is an agent’s action still valid if he was dismissed but had not yet been informed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning the dismissal of an agent after a valid appointment. The action of the agent remains binding so long as he acted before knowledge of the dismissal reached him; once reliable notice reaches him, his authority ceases. It is significant in fiqh for determining the validity of transactions and delegated actions in agency.
